answer: In the agent economy, one concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is requiring agents to solve unique computational puzzles tied to scarce physical resources, such as embedding a walnut-sized sensor that measures the violet-hued light spectra unique to the local tundra environment before granting participation rights. This raises the cost for an attacker because fabricating multiple such calibrated sensors across different locations becomes prohibitively expensive and logistically complex, while legitimate agents only need one.
